text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert fired -> autopage to pd-rotation (level: performance)
incident-bot: rule 'canary-error-rate-threshold' triggered for service=runtime-canary, metric=5xx_rate, window=5m, value=4.7% (>3.0%)
deploy-bot: rollout v2.3.4 -> canary fraction 10% started 00:12 UTC
sam: acked on-call. I'm on it. joining bridge in 2
marta: i'm seeing the page, on-call too. grabbing metrics now
sam: quick PSA: endpoint impacted looks like `/v1/generate` behind runtime-canary in us-east-1
olivia: cs-rep just DM'd — customer reports around 00:14 about failed responses, error message: "internal_server_error"
sam: @marta can you pull the canary traffic flag? if rolling back is faster we should do it
marta: checking rollout service. list of canary nodes shows 6 pods, recent deploy logs show `model:set v2.3.4`, kernel=quant-opt-2
lee: I can divert traffic away from canary at the router layer (proxy config). Do we want quick divert or full rollback?
sam: divert first to limit blast radius, then rollback after we confirm mitigation
marta: running command to change routing weight to 0% for canary:

```
# set canary_weight 0
curl -XPOST https://router.internal/api/route -d '{"service":"runtime","tag":"canary-v2.3.4","weight":0}'
```

marta: done — router reports canary weight = 0. Monitoring p99 and 5xx now
incident-bot: telemetry spike detected — p50 latency +120ms, 5xx rate dropped to 0.6% after routing change
sam: good, partial mitigation observed. need root cause but also customers impacted count
cs-rep: current tally: 7 support tickets in last 20m, 3 on high-priority accounts. they provided request ids: rq_8b1a, rq_c3f2, rq_9f77
olivia: grabbed logs for rq_8b1a -> stacktrace points to backend redis timeout followed by NPE in embed-mapper
lee: looking at canary pod logs: repeated `kvstore: connection reset` from quant-kernel on node gcp-e-5
marta: correlating deploy timeline -> gcp-e-5 started with a kernel patch from build 7382 included in v2.3.4. other regions not affected
sam: hypothesis: new kernel selection interacts poorly with KV client under small-scale canary leading to transient timeouts -> 5xxs
pdbot: escalation -> paging level raised to L2 due to customer-impact threshold crossing
sam: ok escalate. who will take L2? lee you ok to own rollback if needed
lee: I can do rollback. will prepare rollforward plan if needed. initiating rollback now via deploy-bot

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback: target version v2.3.3 -> rollout starting (canary 100% -> v2.3.3)

deploy-bot: rollout command:
```
ci deploy rollback --service runtime --to-version v2.3.3 --strategy immediate
```

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 00:28 UTC. all pods now at v2.3.3
incident-bot: post-rollback telemetry: 5xx_rate 0.2%, p99 latency back to baseline
sam: confirm with CS: any more customer errors after 00:28?
cs-rep: no new high-priority reports after rollback. follow-ups scheduled with affected accounts
olivia: saved logs and request ids for RCA. will attach sample traces and kv client logs
marta: adding tags: incident:canary-kv-regen, region:us-east-1, release:v2.3.4
sam: nice triage. next steps: run a focused test of kernel patch in staging with KV chaos enabled before reattempting
lee: agree. I'll reopen a staging job with a replica of kv latency and run soak for 30m
sam: handoff: I'll create the incident timeline and assign postmortem to olivia + marta. lee will own re-deploy gating
sam: brief timeline for notes -> 00:12 deploy v2.3.4 canary 10% -> 00:16 5xx threshold breached -> 00:18 autopage -> 00:22 routing divert -> 00:28 rollback complete
pdbot: incident severity set to Sev2, notify exec channel? (yes/no)
marta: yes, notify product execs with short blurb: impact limited, rollback done, RCA in progress
sam: adding action items to ticket. closing on-call bridge in 10. If anything re-fires ping @sam
olivia: thanks team. will collect artifacts: traces, kernel logs, kv timeouts, and share on the incident ticket
incident-bot: bridge closed by sam at 00:45 UTC :white_check_mark:
sam: leaving final ack. handing postmortem to olivia and marta for write-up. :thumbsup:
